content.title: What is the Optional Class?
content.description: The Optional class, introduced in Java 8, is a container object that may or may not contain a non-null value. It helps prevent NullPointerException and encourages safer handling of missing values.

content.content: One of the most common runtime errors in Java is the NullPointerException (NPE). The Optional class provides a cleaner and safer alternative to using null. Instead of returning null, methods can return an Optional object that explicitly indicates whether a value is present or absent.

content.title: Why Use Optional?
content.content: Optional reduces the risk of NullPointerException, improves code readability, encourages explicit null handling, and promotes functional programming practices.

steps: No → Return Default or Handle Absence

Key Idea
content.description: An Optional object never stores null directly. Instead, it represents either a present value or an empty container.

content.content: Checking for Values
Before accessing the stored value, developers can check whether the Optional contains a value.

content.title: Best Practice
content.content: Avoid using get() directly unless you're certain a value exists. Prefer methods like orElse(), ifPresent(), or orElseThrow().

content.content: Using orElse()
The orElse() method returns the contained value if present; otherwise, it returns a specified default value.
Using ifPresent()
The ifPresent() method executes a lambda expression only when a value exists.
Optional with Streams
Many stream operations such as findFirst(), findAny(), min(), and max() return Optional objects because the result may not always exist.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Gift Box
content.content: Imagine receiving a gift box. It may contain a present or it may be empty, but the box itself always exists. Optional works the same way—it safely wraps a value that may or may not be present.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Optional, NullPointerException, Optional.of(), Optional.ofNullable(), Optional.empty(), orElse(), orElseGet(), ifPresent(), map(), flatMap(), and Optional with Streams are frequently asked Java interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Should get() be used without checking?
items.answer: No. Calling get() on an empty Optional throws NoSuchElementException.

items.question: Should Optional be used for every field?
items.answer: No. Optional is intended primarily for return types, not class fields or method parameters.

items.question: Can Optional contain null?
items.answer: No. Use Optional.ofNullable() to safely wrap nullable values.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Optional represents the presence or absence of a value, making null handling explicit and reducing runtime errors.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Prefer orElse(), ifPresent(), and orElseThrow() over get().
